summary: The sample implements the core functionality: a Node.js (Mongoose) service that stores bed documents, opens a change stream, maintains per-ward summary documents, seeds data idempotently, and creates a TTL index that targets cleaning-state documents. The build ran against a live cluster and the demo/change-stream exercises updated ward summaries as expected. Key gaps: the change-stream handler does not detect previous→new status transitions (it recomputes counts for the ward on every change), so it does not 'act only on events where the status changed' as required; the handler does not persist resume tokens or checkpoints; there is no retry/backoff handling for transient errors; and the seed script performs many per-bed upserts rather than a batched bulkWrite. Documentation and IaC expectations in the gallery checklist (tests that run without a live cluster, explicit IaC for mongoClusters) are not provided. The TTL index and cleaningExpiresAt semantics are implemented, and the build observed expected TTL-index metadata, but TTL deletions are background-driven and were not observed in a short live test (not a failure of the sample, but a behavioral note).

requirement_results.requirement: A Node.js service uses Mongoose to store bed status documents; each bed doc belongs to a ward and status is one of occupied, available or cleaning.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models/bed.js:4-11 (bed schema with wardId, status enum ['occupied','available','cleaning'])

requirement_results.requirement: The service opens a change stream on the bed status collection and keeps consuming its events while running.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/changeWatcher.js:8-14 (pipeline) and 12 (Bed.watch(..., { fullDocument: 'updateLookup' })) and 58-64 (watcher kept alive until timeout)

requirement_results.requirement: From change stream events detect status transitions and act only on events where the status changed (e.g., compare previous status with new one).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/changeWatcher.js:37-50 (handler recomputes entire ward counts from the Bed collection for every event rather than comparing old/new status or inspecting pre-image)
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Change the change-stream handler to detect transitions. Either enable and use pre-images/fullDocumentBeforeChange or persist the last-known status (or pre-image) and compare to fullDocument.status; then only perform the atomic summary update when status differs.

requirement_results.requirement: A live occupancy summary document is maintained per ward and updated from the change stream handler on every detected transition.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/changeWatcher.js:45-51 (handler recomputes counts and updates WardSummary.updateOne with $set), app/src/models/wardSummary.js:4-12 (schema)
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Change handler to compute the delta from the transition and apply a targeted atomic update (see next). If you prefer full recompute, still make it conditional on observed status change to reduce work.

requirement_results.requirement: Each summary update is a single atomic update operation (e.g., one updateOne with $inc adjusting the affected counts).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/changeWatcher.js:50 (await WardSummary.updateOne({ wardId }, { $set: { counts } }, { upsert: true })) — single updateOne call, which is atomic for a single document

requirement_results.requirement: A TTL index is created in code on a Date field of the bed documents, with expireAfterSeconds (or the indexed Date value) derived from a configurable cleaning timeout.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/seed.js:12-16 (createIndex({ cleaningExpiresAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 0 })), app/src/seed.js:34-41 (cleaningExpiresAt set using DEFAULT_TTL derived from CLEANING_TTL_SECONDS)

requirement_results.requirement: Cleaning-state documents, and only those, are expired by the TTL index once the timeout has passed (e.g., set/clear the Date when entering/leaving cleaning or use a partial filter).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/server.js:25-31 (sets cleaningExpiresAt when status==='cleaning' and clears it otherwise), app/src/seed.js:38-41 (seed sets cleaningExpiresAt only for cleaning), app/src/models/bed.js:9-10 (cleaningExpiresAt field)

requirement_results.requirement: Connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in repo.
A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.js:8-16 (singleton connection variable and connect() that returns existing connection)

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/seed.js:12-16 (index creation) and 34-41 (updateOne upsert per bed) and 30-32 (WardSummary upsert with $setOnInsert)

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in a dependency lock so installs are reproducible.
requirement_results.evidence: app/package.json:18-22 (dependencies with ^ ranges), app/package-lock.json present in repo (package-lock.json at project root)
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Either pin exact versions in package.json (remove ^) or rely on package-lock.json and document that CI uses package-lock for deterministic installs.

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: No tests or test harness present in repository (no test files found during discovery).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a small unit test suite that uses an in-memory Mongo replacement or mocks Mongoose (e.g., mongodb-memory-server or sinon to stub model methods) that runs without a live cluster.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No IaC files found (no Bicep/Terraform templates) in repository; builder intentionally used existing cluster per decision D004.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a minimal Bicep template (or Terraform) showing Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters example (documentdb-azure-deployment skill has canonical templates).

requirement_results.requirement: README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md includes what the sample shows, prerequisites and quickstart (seed/demo/server) but lacks an explicit clean-up section for sample-created data/indexes.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a 'Clean-up' section to README describing how to remove seeded documents/indexes or how to drop the sample database/collections (e.g., mongosh commands or MCP commands).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name 'Azure DocumentDB' throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md:1 and other files refer to 'Azure DocumentDB' (no Cosmos DB or Amazon DocumentDB names present)

checks.practice: Create a single MongoClient (or single Mongoose connection) and reuse it for the process lifetime instead of creating a client per request.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js:8-16 (singleton connection variable and connect() that returns existing connection)

checks.practice: Tune connection-pool parameters for your environment: use small pools for serverless, larger pools for long-running OLTP, set minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS and serverSelectionTimeoutMS appropriately.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js:14-21 (only serverSelectionTimeoutMS set; no explicit pool size/minIdle/maxIdle configuration)
checks.fix: Set pool options (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS) in mongoose.connect options or document expected production values in README (e.g., maxPoolSize:50 for OLTP).

checks.practice: Always require TLS on the wire (tls=true) and do not disable certificate validation in production; configure TLS options only via environment/secret-driven config for local detours.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example:3 (connection string example includes tls=true); app/src/db.js:19-21 (comment notes TLS/auth options are usually encoded in the connection string)

checks.practice: Persist change-stream resume tokens durably and resume change streams using resumeAfter / startAtOperationTime so a watcher can continue from the last-processed event after restart.
checks.evidence: app/src/changeWatcher.js shows Bed.watch(...) usage but no durable storage or persistence of resume tokens; there is no control collection or checkpoint logic.
checks.fix: Persist the change._id (resume token) or last processed clusterTime into a small control collection after each processed event; on restart, open the stream with resumeAfter: savedToken.

checks.practice: When you need the post-update document in change-stream events use fullDocument: 'updateLookup' so update events include the current document state.
Enable pre-images (changeStreamPreAndPostImages) on a collection if you need fullDocumentBeforeChange, but be aware this increases storage and write amplification.
checks.evidence: app/src/changeWatcher.js does not attempt to use fullDocumentBeforeChange; the sample uses fullDocument: 'updateLookup' and recompute logic instead

checks.practice: Use a TTL index on a Date field (createIndex({ expiresAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 0 })) to expire at a specific timestamp, and ensure the field is a Date (not a number); know TTL deletions are background-driven and can be delayed.
checks.evidence: app/src/seed.js:12-16 (createIndex({ cleaningExpiresAt:1 }, { expireAfterSeconds:0 })), app/src/models/bed.js:9-10 (cleaningExpiresAt is Date)

checks.practice: Do not rely on TTL for strict, immediate deletion semantics; if you need deterministic deletion timing implement an explicit scheduled job or background worker.
checks.evidence: app/src/ttl_check.js demonstrates a short TTL test and README/seed note documents that TTL deletions are background-driven; run logs show TTL deletion not observed in 30s

checks.practice: Design compound indexes using ESR and create a compound index like { wardId: 1, status: 1 } to support queries listing beds by ward and status.
checks.evidence: app/src/models/bed.js:15 (BedSchema.index({ wardId: 1, status: 1 })), app/src/seed.js:16 (also creates the compound index)

checks.practice: Denormalize read-heavy data and precompute small per-ward summary documents (one document per ward) to avoid expensive $lookup and permit efficient atomic updates.
checks.evidence: app/src/models/wardSummary.js:4-12 (WardSummary schema), app/src/seed.js:30-32 (creates summary docs), app/src/changeWatcher.js:45-50 (updates summary)

checks.practice: Use findAndModify / findOneAndUpdate (atomic single-document modification) for counters and other atomic updates to a single document (supports upsert and $inc semantics).
checks.evidence: app/src/changeWatcher.js:50 uses WardSummary.updateOne(..., { upsert: true }) which performs a single-document atomic update (the sample uses $set of counts rather than $inc delta)

checks.practice: Design change-stream consumers to be idempotent (dedupe or use idempotency keys) because event replays or redelivery are possible and can otherwise cause double-counting.
checks.evidence: app/src/changeWatcher.js recomputes counts on each event which happens to be idempotent in effect, but there is no public DocumentDB page for the specific recommended dedupe pattern in this service; practice basis is prior knowledge.
checks.searched: Searched: 'Azure DocumentDB change stream duplicate', 'Azure DocumentDB change stream idempotent'
checks.what_would_help: A public guidance page documenting recommended idempotency/dedupe patterns for DocumentDB change-stream consumers (control-collection + processed-event id checkpoint example).

checks.practice: For secrets and developer workflows include a .env.example with a placeholder DOCUMENTDB_URI and instruct developers not to commit real credentials; in CI use environment secrets or Key Vault.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example:1-10 (placeholder DOCUMENTDB_URI and CLEANING_TTL_SECONDS explained) and README.md:14-16 (copy .env.example to .env)

checks.practice: Use the DocumentDB MCP or mongosh explain/index/list commands to validate index usage and get collection/index statistics before making index changes.
checks.evidence: events.jsonl: documentdb_list_indexes result (index list for beds) and documentdb_list_databases show collections; the builder used MCP tooling during verification (documentdb_list_indexes call recorded).

decision_reviews.comment: D001 records an operator approval ('ready_with_gaps') with no evidence or tool trace beyond the decision entry. The events log contains the decision entry but no external artifact to verify the operator's stated readiness criteria.
D002: The decision to use Node.js with Mongoose 7.x is recorded and matches package.json which declares mongoose ^7.6.0. events.jsonl contains the log_decision entry (Recorded as D002).

D003: The decision text records using tls=true, SCRAM-SHA-256 and retryWrites=false. The events log shows D003 recorded. The code relies on the connection string to carry TLS/auth options (app/src/db.js:14-21) and .env.example includes a tls=true example. This is acceptable, but the decision implies client options would be set explicitly; the code doesn't enforce them, so the decision is somewhat optimistic about how options are supplied.

D004: Decision to not provision Azure resources is consistent with the run environment and events; the builder used an existing DOCUMENTDB_URI and did not execute IaC provisioning (events show no az resource create or IaC writes).

D005 states the summary will be updated atomically via $inc upsert. The events show D005 was recorded, but the implementation in app/src/changeWatcher.js recomputes counts and uses updateOne with $set of the counts (app/src/changeWatcher.js:45-50) rather than applying a delta via $inc based on the observed transition. The decision content and the code therefore diverge.

D006: Decision to use TTL index on cleaningExpiresAt with expireAfterSeconds:0 and set that field when entering cleaning is implemented: seed.js creates the index and server.js/demo/seed set/clear cleaningExpiresAt accordingly. events.jsonl shows the index metadata via documentdb_list_indexes.

D007: The decision to perform a live TTL test was executed — events.jsonl contains the run of src/ttl_check.js and output showing TTL deletion was not observed within 30s. The decision and evidence align.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Guidance and example tests showing how to unit-test DocumentDB/Mongoose code without a live cluster (preferred patterns: mongodb-memory-server, fakered/mocks, or MCP gateway-based tests).
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-local-deployment skill, overall agent skills for DocumentDB, repository files (no tests found).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: No unit tests were added; the sample contains runtime verification steps that require a live cluster. This reduces confidence for CI and reviewers and increases the manual verification burden.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short page 'Testing DocumentDB samples offline' that includes: 1) an example using mongodb-memory-server with Mongoose and instructions to wire it into the sample's connect() during tests; 2) a small Jest test that stubs change stream events and asserts WardSummary updates; 3) an alternative using the DocumentDB Gateway Docker image and instructions and npm scripts to run integration tests. Include code snippets and a sample package.json test script.

doc_gaps.topic: Provide a minimal Bicep example for mongoClusters
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A tiny IaC quickstart (Bicep or Terraform) showing how to provision a Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters resource with minimal, cost-conscious defaults (tier, region, storage).
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-azure-deployment skill and Microsoft Learn templates; the sample repo contained no IaC files.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The gallery sample has no IaC attachment; authors and users may target the wrong resource type (databaseAccounts) if they follow older Cosmos DB instructions. This increases the chance of provisioning the wrong service or producing an unprovisioned expectation gap.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A tiny 'iac/mongoCluster.bicep' example (parameters: location, sku/tier, serverVersion) plus short README text showing az deployment group create with the template, and a note: 'Use Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters — do not use databaseAccounts for vCore DocumentDB'.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A concrete example that shows persisting resume tokens (change._id) into a small control collection and using resumeAfter when reopening the stream, including sample code for Mongoose/native driver.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Change-stream docs in Microsoft Learn and documentdb skills; public docs describe resume tokens but lack a short 'store and resume' code example for Mongoose-based watchers.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample's change-stream watcher does not persist resume tokens; if the watcher restarts it may reprocess events and the sample lacks a durable checkpoint example for authors to copy.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: An agent-kit rule and a short code snippet: 1) after processing an event, write { watcherId, lastResumeToken, lastProcessedTs } to a control collection; 2) on startup, query control collection and pass resumeAfter: token to collection.watch(); include failure/retry semantics and expected schema for the control document.

doc_gaps.topic: Idempotent consumer pattern for DocumentDB change streams
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A DocumentDB-specific example of idempotent change-stream consumption (dedupe/inbox pattern, uniqueness constraints, or per-event checkpointing) demonstrating how to avoid double-counting when events are replayed or reordered in multi-shard deployments.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Azure architecture patterns (Idempotent Consumer) and change-stream docs; there is conceptual guidance but no short DocumentDB-oriented sample.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample's recompute approach is idempotent by accident; other apps might implement naive $inc deltas and would be at risk of double-counting without idempotency guidance.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A 'Change-stream consumer patterns' page showing 1) full-recompute approach (pros/cons), 2) delta-$inc with pre-images or stored previous-state approach, and 3) dedupe/inbox table pattern, each with small code snippets using Mongoose/native driver.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A short naming/disambiguation note explaining that Azure DocumentDB (vCore/mongoClusters) is billed by compute tier (M-sizes) and not by Cosmos DB RUs, and list the recommended metrics to monitor for DocumentDB clusters (CPU, memory, IOPS, connections) plus pointers to slow-query logging and explain-based analysis.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-monitoring skill and Microsoft Learn; agent readiness found confusion in cold answers.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Risk that authors will monitor or reason about RUs (a Cosmos DB concept) and misinterpret cluster health or plan scaling incorrectly.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A one-paragraph callout on the main quickstart: 'Azure DocumentDB (mongoClusters) uses vCore compute tiers (Mxx) and is not RU-based — monitor CPU/memory/IOPS and enable diagnostic settings + slow-query logs. See sample monitoring checklist.'
